claims.claim: A Node process using a lean WebSocket library such as ws or uWebSockets.js can hold tens of thousands of mostly idle connections
claims.why: The benchmarks don't test WebSockets or ws/uWebSockets.js, and the largest connection count measured is 256, nowhere near tens of thousands.

claims.claim: 50k clients heartbeating every 30 seconds is about 1,700 messages a second, which is trivial for Node
claims.measured: node-express 17,601 req/s and node-fastify 40,730 req/s plaintext on 1 CPU; node-express 14,188 req/s in the 10 ms I/O-wait test
claims.why: One Node core measured 10–24 times that rate in HTTP requests, which cost more than heartbeat messages, so calling 1,700/s trivial fits the data.

claims.measured: go-gin 8–16 MB and go-nethttp 7–15 MB peak memory, against node-express 55–75 MB and node-fastify 57–77 MB; idle 2 MB against 38–43 MB
claims.why: Go used about 4–7 times less memory than Node in every test, so 'memory-efficient' is supported.

claims.claim: At 50k connections Go gains little over Node
claims.measured: I/O wait at 256 connections: go-gin 20,235 req/s and 16 MB against node-fastify 17,462 req/s and 69 MB, and node-express 14,188 req/s and 68 MB; plaintext: go-gin 53,941 against fastify 40,730 and express 17,601
claims.why: Nothing was measured with 50k WebSocket connections; the closest test shows Go only 1.2–1.4 times Node's throughput, but with about 4 times less memory, so the data can't settle the claim at that scale.
